findings.finding: All 3366 rows replay exactly on the validator's instrumented build (every printed field except ms: I, M, S, H, L, N, ok, every phase snapshot and arm extra); a 51-row nonce sample (1 per arm-parameter x bits, 17 at 32 bits) on a pristine build from the frozen source and a 17-row nonce sample on the producer's binary (sha256 c55c87dd..., equal to bin_sha256 of every row) match too. 153 dumped runs (one nonce-drawn configuration per cell, all 17 runs) carry 1,096,704 recovered logs: every one equals the planted log, Q_t is on the curve and [log]G = Q_t under the validator's own Jacobian EC code (64,504 distinct scalar multiplications; negative controls reject off-by-one and negated logs); the planted lists are identical across the 17 runs of each configuration. 0 failures.

The v5 harness is the v4 harness (bb3d2bc40e) plus the v4 validator's patch_ic5rw.py and patch_rhodpu.py arms plus the N counter, and nothing else: after whitespace normalisation the only differences are the cn field, fn native(), the native() calls (rho-family hidx x4, rhodp/rhodpu canon x2 each, ic5w/ic5rw W-step x1 each) and the N output field; rustfmt reflowed the closures it touched. Empirically the v5 binary reproduces I, M, S, H, L and ok of 72 nonce-drawn v4 rows (ic5, ic5ks, rho2xks, rhodp, bsgs2 from the v4 holdout; ic5w, ic5rw, rhodpu from the v4 validator's sensitivity runs) and its N equals the v4 validator's instrumented step-index counts (rho2xks) and 2 x canonicalisation counts (rhodp) in 18 of 18 rows with such counts. On the v5 holdout the instrumented replay confirms in every row: N = step-index calls (rho2xks, 932,642,597 in total), N = 2 x canonicalisations (rhodpu, 2 x 2,770,912,573), N = W-step indices (ic5w 287,272; ic5rw 239,813), N = 0 for ic5, ic5ks and bsgs2; H = HashMap calls in every row of ic5, ic5w, rho2xks, rhodpu and bsgs2. 'Two per generated point' for rhodpu is right for this code: each generated point is canonicalised once and its x is mixed into one 64-bit value whose bits give the step index, the look-ahead test and the DP test (the code evaluates that same mix 5.25e9 + 2.62e9 times, i.e. three times per point; an implementation needs it once). The IC trials do only xpair (counted I, M, S) and table probes (counted H): there is no per-trial index, canonicalisation or other native step; the W offsets are shared by all targets (ic5/ic5ks arithmetic progression with no index; ic5w/ic5rw one counted index per W). No free information: the planted logs are used only to plant the targets (uncounted field copy) and in the final counted check; ic5rw's retained hits use only logs it has already solved.

scripts/recompute.py (validator code, from runs.json) reproduces all 972 entries of summary.json and all 972 of summary_v4rule.json with maximum relative difference 0, every decision of analysis.txt and analysis_v4rule.txt, and (independent numpy bootstrap, B = 20000) the same decisions. icbest vs rhobest: unranked 27 (5a rule), dearer 27 (v4 rule); vs bsgs2 dearer 27; ic5rw vs rhobest unranked 27. I = 10M ranges: 1.0633-1.1586 (h = 0, lower bound > 1 in 9/9), 0.9983-1.0539 (h = 0.1, lower bound > 1 in 8/9), 0.7135-0.7995 (h = 1, upper bound < 1 in 9/9); in all 27 (cell, cI) the lower bound is > 1 at h = 0 and the upper bound < 1 at h = 1. v4 rule at I = 10M 1.0475-2.0184; icbest/bsgs2 1.1114-1.4709. The 108 numbers of the RESULTS table and the 27 of noverify.txt match. Shared verification phase 34.5-47.4 GAE per target at I = 10M in every arm.

Three statements in RESULTS.md are not supported: (a) 'Rho: rho2xks at every price, in all 198 configurations; rhodpu never': at I = 10M, h = 1 rhodpu is the cheapest rho in 4 of 198 configurations (all 32 b, T = 1024; by 0.2-0.7%), and at I = 3M, h = 1 in 27 of 198; (b) 'At h = 1 the best kappa is interior': kappa = 0.5, the top of the frozen grid, is best in 36 of 198 (the conclusion that the h = 1 result does not rest on the grid edge is nevertheless right, V5-F6); (c) noverify 'h = 1: 0.71-0.73': the minimum is 0.70499 (32 b, T = 16384), so 0.70-0.73. No headline number is affected.

findings.check: 5 robustness of 'IC cheaper at h = 1 in all 9 cells'
findings.finding: The h = 1 result is a property of the pricing convention, which the protocol pre-registered and which matches AGENTS.md 5a and ecbench's counters (canonicalisations_uncharged per point and partition_hashes_uncharged per step, priced separately; ecbench's negation_strong also charges dp_tests_uncharged, which v5 does not). Within such conventions it is robust: rho2xks's step index priced 0 (it could reuse the hash of the per-point table lookup): IC/rho at h = 1, I = 10M 0.870-0.918, unranked 27; only restart starts charged: 0.863-0.908; rho2xks index doubled: 0.644-0.716; rhodpu at 4 per point (v4 validator's count): unchanged. It is not robust to charging a distinguished-point rho one native operation per point instead of two (canonicalisation or point hash taken as free): then rhodpu is the cheapest rho at h = 1 in all 198 configurations, IC/rho at h = 1, I = 10M is 0.833-1.059 (28 b T = 1024 0.991 [0.984, 1.002], 32 b T = 4096 1.010 [1.008, 1.013], 32 b T = 1024 1.059 [1.043, 1.065]), the IC is cheaper at h = 1 in only 19 of 27 (cell, cI), and 3 decisions become dearer (32 b T = 1024 at I = 10M and 30M, 32 b T = 4096 at I = 10M); with rho2xks's index free as well, 7 dearer and 20 unranked. Under that reading the IC's h = 1 ratio also grows with the group (T = 1024, I = 10M: 0.908, 0.991, 1.059 at 24, 28, 32 b), whereas under the frozen convention it does not (0.748, 0.731, 0.728). RESULTS' Limits mentions only that 2 per point favours rho over the v4 validator's 4.

Validator panels (not pre-registered; 792 runs, every target verified by the harness): rho2xks at kappa 0.75 and 1.0 on all 198 configurations is never the cheapest rho at any price under the frozen convention (decisions and ranges unchanged), so the h = 1 result does not rest on the top grid edge; rho2xks's h = 0 optimum at the floor (0.05 in 126/198) can only make rho cheaper at h = 0, which widens the IC's h = 0 loss and cannot change an unranked decision. rho2x without retention at kappa 0.5 and 1.0 never wins under the frozen convention (it wins 110/198 at h = 1 only when rho2xks's index is free, where the IC stays at 0.875-0.919). A modelled distinguished-point rho without the negation map (one native operation per point, sqrt 2 more walk work; a model from rhodpu's kappa = 0 phases, not a measurement) wins 38/198 at h = 1 but leaves the ranges and all 27 decisions unchanged. Cross-fitting every arm's parameter choice on the other seed (removing the min-of-10 vs min-of-4 selection asymmetry): unranked 27, I = 10M ranges 1.0632-1.1518 / 0.9948-1.0418 / 0.7147-0.8018. Counting the retention IC arms' two probes per trial class (ret and table) as two hash operations: unranked 27, h = 0.1 range 1.035-1.077, h = 1 unchanged. A standard pseudo-random-walk rho cannot avoid a per-step partition decision; the generic method with no per-step native work in this panel is BSGS, which the IC does not beat at any price (1.11-1.47x).

Uncounted on the rho side: the walk-restart RNG draws (rho2xks 32,384,938 = 3.5% of steps; rhodpu 144,400,826 = 5.2% of points), which favours rho. Uncounted on both sides: F_p and mod-n additions and the solver's zero tests, by the harness's stated convention. Undercounted for the IC: ic5ks/ic5rw count one H for the retained-table and table probe of one x (merged-table equivalent; the instrumented replay shows 0 <= H - HashMap calls <= targets in all 396 such rows); counting both changes no decision (V5-F6). The IC's mu = 1.0 is frozen from v3 and not re-tuned for h = 1 (favours rho).

Freeze order holds: PROTOCOL.md, run.py, analyze.py, noverify.py, mk_runs.py, plot.py, the instances and the harness are in 5aab996e55 (03:11:47Z) and unchanged through 2729e252e2; the bench record shows the holdout started at 03:12:01Z; the rows record commit 59e4e892b3 (bench-record-only). Gaps: rows.jsonl (2,547,056 bytes, .jsonl) is committed to Git instead of the artifact store (AGENTS.md 13; the bench record at 1f85ca3678 lists it with uploaded: false); the bench record at the validated commit is open with no commands, metrics or raw data (1f85ca3678 adds them; closed_utc still null); the leaderboard builder was pointed at v5 (1f85ca3678) before this validation; the smoke runs behind the protocol's predictions (instances, seeds, outputs) are not committed.

All 33 curves are valid (p and n prime, nonsingular, G and the fixture point on the curve, nG = O, n the only multiple of n in the Hasse interval so #E = n, fixture log correct) and regenerate byte-identically (33 files and MANIFEST.json) from gen_instances.py --families W --bits 24,28,32 --per 11 --seed mtfo-v5-20261112. 0 (p, a, b) overlap with 116,860 curve records in 107,880 JSON files under research/ and docs/curves. One (p, n) coincidence: v5 W32-4 has the same p and group order as v4 W32-4 but a different j-invariant (not isomorphic; a different curve and different targets).

accepted_results_headline: On 33 fresh prime-order curves (group orders about 2^24-2^32, T = 1024-16384, 22 paired configurations per cell), with counted field and mod-n operations and every arm's hash-table and native work (rho step indices, distinguished-point canonicalisations and point hashes, IC offset-step indices) priced at h = 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE each, the cheapest of four multi-target IC variants is unranked against the cheapest of ten runs of this harness's multi-target rho in all 27 (cell, I/M) decisions because the order flips with h: at I = 10 M it is 1.06-1.16x at h = 0 (dearer in all 9 cells), 1.00-1.05x at h = 0.1 and 0.71-0.80x at h = 1 (cheaper in all 9 cells). With native work unpriced it is dearer in all 27 (1.05-2.02x at I = 10 M); it is 1.11-1.47x a paired BSGS at every price. The h = 1 advantage rests on charging a distinguished-point rho two native operations per point: at one per point the IC is not cheaper at h = 1 at 28-32 bits with T = 1024-4096 (0.83-1.06x at I = 10 M) and 3 of the 27 decisions become dearer.
